issues.t: Upper ball joint wear and separation (recall 04V-596)
issues.sym: A clunk from the front end over bumps, loose or wandering steering, and in the worst case a front wheel that suddenly tucks in.
issues.why: Water can get into the front upper ball joints, push out the grease and corrode them. The worn joint can eventually pull apart.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. If the front end clunks or the steering feels loose, have the ball joints inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Exterior lights can fail from timer module fault (recall 02V-322)
issues.sym: Headlights or other exterior lights stop working or act erratically.
issues.why: A fault in the central timer module, which controls the lights, can shut them off.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and avoid night driving until the lights work reliably.

issues.t: Windshield wiper motor can quit (recall 04V-216)
issues.sym: The wipers slow down, stop partway, or stop working in the rain.
issues.why: The wiper module motor can fail, leaving the driver without clear vision.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the wiper motor replaced if it is open.

issues.t: Power outlet connector short and fire risk (recall 06V-339)
issues.sym: A hot plastic or burning smell near the power outlets, or an outlet that stops working.
issues.why: High resistance can build up in the power outlet wiring connector and overheat it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. If you smell burning plastic, stop using the outlets and have the wiring inspected right away.

issues.t: Instrument panel fire risk from gauge cluster circuit (recalls 03V-528, 07V-092)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from behind the dash, flickering dash or interior lights, or a gauge cluster that goes dark.
issues.why: A circuit inside the instrument cluster that powers the interior lights can overheat. An earlier recall on 2004 models addressed a cracked part on the same circuit board.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both recalls. If you smell burning from the dash, pull over, shut the vehicle off and have it towed for inspection.

issues.t: Battery cable can chafe and short (recall 04V-578)
issues.sym: A burning smell under the hood, a sudden loss of electrical power, or a no-start.
issues.why: A battery cable can rub against nearby parts until its insulation wears through and it shorts, which can start an under-hood fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the cable routing inspected if it is open.

issues.t: Throttle cable can stick open (recall 04V-020)
issues.sym: The engine keeps revving or the vehicle keeps pulling after you lift off the gas pedal.
issues.why: The throttle control cable can bind so the throttle does not return to idle.
issues.next: If the throttle sticks, shift to neutral, brake firmly and pull over. Check the VIN for the recall before driving again.

issues.t: Vehicle may roll away in Park (recall 05V-460)
issues.sym: The vehicle creeps or rolls after being shifted into Park, especially on a slope.
issues.why: A cup plug inside the automatic transmission can come loose and keep the park mechanism from holding.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and check the VIN for the recall right away.

issues.t: ABS control module needs reprogramming (recall 05V-554)
issues.sym: ABS or brake warning lights, or unusual brake or stability behavior.
issues.why: A software fault in the anti-lock brake module could affect vehicle control without warning.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the module reprogrammed before relying on the vehicle in slippery conditions.

issues.t: Rear Watts link can fail (recall 06V-240)
issues.sym: A clunk from the rear suspension, or the rear end feeling loose or shifting side to side.
issues.why: A part of the rear Watts link suspension, which keeps the axle centered, can fail and affect handling.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the rear suspension inspected before highway driving.

issues.t: Windshield wiper motor can stop working (recall 06V-067)
issues.sym: The wipers stop working in some conditions.
issues.why: The front wiper motor can lose its ability to wipe, which blocks the driver's view in bad weather.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the wiper motor replaced if it is open.

issues.t: Fuel pump relay failure in the power module (recalls)
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or it stalls while driving.
issues.why: The fuel pump relay inside the under-hood power module (TIPM) can fail. Several recalls cover affected vehicles, including a follow-up for some that already had the first fix.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the power module inspected if the vehicle stalls or won't start.

issues.t: Brake booster corrosion (recalls)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal that takes more effort to stop the vehicle, especially in freezing weather.
issues.why: Water can get into the brake booster and corrode it, reducing power assist. The water can also freeze inside it. Recalls added a shield and later rechecked it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recalls and have the brakes inspected right away if the pedal feels hard.

issues.t: Alternator failure (recalls)
issues.sym: A battery or charging warning light, dimming lights, a burning smell, and then a sudden stall.
issues.why: The alternator can fail internally without warning. On some vehicles a failing alternator can also short and start a fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Get to safety and have the charging system tested if the battery light comes on.

issues.t: Left cylinder head valve seat problem (warranty extension)
issues.sym: A ticking noise from the engine, a rough idle or misfire, and a check engine light, usually pointing to cylinder 2.
issues.why: A valve seat in the left cylinder head could wear or loosen on some early Pentastar engines. Chrysler extended the warranty on the left head for affected vehicles.
issues.next: Have the misfire diagnosed soon and ask the dealer whether the head warranty extension applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Oil filter housing and oil cooler leaks
issues.sym: Oil pooling at the back of the engine, a burning oil smell, coolant loss, or oil and coolant mixing.
issues.why: The plastic oil filter housing that also holds the oil cooler can crack or its gaskets can leak after many heat cycles.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and the housing replaced. Do not let oil drip onto hot exhaust parts.

issues.t: Lifter and camshaft wear
issues.sym: A ticking sound that does not go away when warm, misfires, a rough idle and a check engine light.
issues.why: Lifters can stop rolling and wear the camshaft lobes. It is widely reported and was the subject of a lawsuit, but there is no recall.
issues.next: Have a ticking Hemi checked quickly. Early repair limits the damage to the camshaft.

issues.t: ABS module fault (recalls)
issues.sym: ABS and stability control warning lights, brake lights that stay on, or the shifter leaving Park without pressing the brake.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake module can develop a fault that affects several systems. A later recall replaced the earlier fix.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have it repaired soon.

issues.t: Steering rack can bind (recall 22V-154)
issues.sym: Steering feels stiff, sticky or notchy, especially at low speed.
issues.why: The steering rack bar may not have been properly hardened, which can cause binding. Dealers replace the steering gear.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and stop driving if the steering becomes hard to turn.

issues.t: Rear spoiler can crack and come loose (recalls)
issues.sym: Rubbing or a gap at the roof spoiler when the liftgate opens, or cracked spoiler edges.
issues.why: The rear spoiler may sit out of line with the roof, so the liftgate hits it when opened. A damaged spoiler can fly off on the road.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recalls and have a cracked spoiler repaired before highway driving.
